name: Allied Body Works Inc
old_description: Since 1949, Allied Body has been taking care of the tradespeople who make the world go-round.
about:
Allied Body Works Inc. has operated from Seattle, Washington since 1949, when Charles Walter Bull and two partners each invested $200 to leave Heiser Body and open a small garage on Fourth Avenue. The company remains family‑owned; after passing through the Bull and Minice lines, Charles’s great‑grandson Adam Keane purchased the business in February 2023 and serves as president.

Today the shop at 625 South 96th Street builds and installs custom truck bodies and upfit solutions for light‑ to medium‑duty vehicles. Services span cargo‑van interiors, service bodies, dump bodies, platform bodies, pickup‑truck accessories, liftgates, cranes, electrical and lighting packages, and the proprietary Walker Blocker side‑guard system. The team of roughly a dozen technicians also handles fabrication, repair, and emerging EV upfit work, serving the greater Pacific Northwest.

Customers include tradespeople, mobile workforces, fleet operators, and government agencies. Early work included armored cars for Loomis; later the company expanded with Seattle’s shipping and distribution sector. Current accounts range from local contractors to municipal fleets needing van upfitting, truck side guards, and turnkey work‑truck packages.

The founders’ original commitment to honest work and fair treatment still drives the culture. Allied emphasizes quick turnaround — meeting deadlines is a stated priority — and the ability to execute complex, one‑off designs. A future‑focused mindset adds safety innovations like the Walker Blocker and green options such as solar‑integrated upfits.
